errors.text_span: of various large language models (LLMs) in the ABS-AOS pattern
errors.evidence: This information is derived from the paper's caption, not the visual elements of the chart itself. A description should focus on what is visually depicted.

errors.text_span: arranged from left to right in descending order of performance
errors.evidence: The bars are not arranged in descending order. For example, the first bar is 61.09%, the second is 48.28%, the third is 24.64%, and the fourth is 60.72%.

errors.text_span: The tallest bar on the far left reaches 61.09%, followed by 60.72%, then 54.83%, 48.83%, 48.28%, 46.36%, 44.09%, 43.79%, 43.54%, and the shortest bar at 24.64% on the far right.
errors.evidence: This sentence incorrectly describes the sequence of bars by listing them in descending order of value, not their actual left-to-right position on the chart. For instance, the second bar from the left is 48.28%, not 60.72%. It also incorrectly places the shortest bar (24.64%) on the 'far right' when it is the third bar from the left.

errors.text_span: According to the caption, these performances are stratified into three tiers based on the global mean performance (OP_{GM}): Tier-1 includes models with OP_{GM} in [55, 61], Tier-2 in [41, 49], and Tier-3 in [25, 27].
errors.evidence: This entire sentence is an interpretation of external information from the caption, not a description of what is visually present in the chart.

errors.text_span: The chart visually groups models by performance level, with the first two bars (61.09% and 60.72%) falling into Tier-1, the next five bars (54.83% down to 43.79%) falling into Tier-2, and the last two bars (43.54% and 24.64%) falling into Tier-3.
errors.evidence: The chart contains no 'visual groups'. This structure is invented. Furthermore, the assignment of values to bar positions is incorrect, as it is based on the false premise that the bars are sorted by value. For example, the first two bars are 61.09% and 48.28%, not 61.09% and 60.72%.
The description fails to mention the total number of bars in the chart, which is 12.
